title: The Alps Mountain Range
text: The Alps are the highest and most extensive mountain range system in Europe, stretching approximately 1,200 km across eight countries: France, Switzerland, Monaco, Italy, Liechtenstein, Austria, Germany, and Slovenia. The highest peak is Mont Blanc at 4,808 meters, on the border between France and Italy. The Alps were formed by the collision of the African and Eurasian tectonic plates and are geologically young mountains. They are a source of the Rhine, Rhône, Po, and Inn rivers. The Alps are a major hub for winter sports, attracting millions of tourists annually. They also have historical significance as a natural barrier that has influenced migration, warfare, and cultural exchange throughout European history.
